title: FDS engine configuration
description: The single repo-root config.json consumed by the fds engine. Every field is optional: missing fields fall back to the engine defaults (crates/fds-core/src/config.rs). Hardware-derived defaults are produced by fds-detect (D-1 socket-buffer sizing from measured L3; worker count follows logical CPUs).

pin_cores.description: Pin each worker thread to its own logical CPU.
pin_cores.x-trade-off: Removes scheduler migration and cache thrash; consumes whole CPUs. Disable when cores are shared with other tenants.

threads.description: Worker thread count; 0 = one per logical CPU.
threads.x-trade-off: More workers give more parallelism but per-core caches and queues must fit; oversubscription adds scheduling noise (see the measured p999 tails in WIKI.md).
threads.x-derived-from: engine default (0 = one per logical CPU; 2x physical on SMT)

stack_bytes.description: Worker thread stack size, in bytes.
stack_bytes.x-trade-off: Larger stacks waste address space; smaller risks overflow in deep call paths (pool buffers are heap-backed).

strategy.description: Polling strategy: epoll-busy-poll (classic readiness loop, busy-poll to empty) or io-uring (kernel-side submission/completion batching).
strategy.x-trade-off: epoll is the proven baseline; io-uring amortizes syscalls at high packet rates but its SQPOLL thread needs privileges and newer kernels for best results.

max_events.description: Preallocated event array capacity per reactor.
max_events.x-trade-off: Too small drops events per drain; too large wastes memory per worker.

busy_poll.description: Busy-poll the ready queue to empty before yielding.
busy_poll.x-trade-off: Lowest latency at the cost of CPU spin when idle; disable on shared CPUs.

timeout_ms.description: Poll timeout in milliseconds when not busy-polling.
timeout_ms.x-trade-off: 0 with busy-poll off blocks indefinitely; a small timeout bounds wake latency at the cost of syscall rate.

io_uring_entries.x-trade-off: Larger rings hold more in-flight ops; entries are power-of-two and floored by the datapath (UDP slots + accept + timeout).

io_uring_sq_thread.description: io_uring SQPOLL thread CPU; 0 = no SQPOLL (plain ring).
io_uring_sq_thread.x-trade-off: SQPOLL removes submission syscalls but needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN; the ring falls back to a plain ring when creation is rejected.

rcvbuf.description: SO_RCVBUF per UDP socket, in bytes.
rcvbuf.x-trade-off: Larger absorbs bursts and jumbo datagrams at the cost of memory; sized from the L3 budget by fds-detect.
rcvbuf.x-derived-from: D-1 (L3-aware buffer sizing; fds-detect derives from measured L3)

sndbuf.description: SO_SNDBUF per UDP socket, in bytes.
sndbuf.x-trade-off: Larger absorbs bursts at the cost of memory; the kernel doubles the value it reports.

gso_segment_size.x-trade-off: Fewer, larger sends amortize syscalls but the kernel must segment each; 0 keeps software segmentation.

gro.x-trade-off: Fewer receive completions at the cost of per-flow reassembly state.

zerocopy.x-trade-off: Avoids a kernel copy for big buffers at the cost of completion-notification handling and page pinning.

reuseport.x-trade-off: Enables per-core distribution; the option must be set before bind for reuseport-group admission (the engine does this).

incoming_cpu.x-trade-off: Pins flows to the RX softirq CPU — on loopback that collapses every flow onto one worker; enable only with NIC RSS/IRQ affinity (WIKI.md).

nodelay.x-trade-off: Disables Nagle; tiny writes become small packets, correct for a latency-bound echo.

quickack.x-trade-off: Fewer delayed-ACK stalls at the cost of more ACK traffic.

defer_accept.x-trade-off: Defers accept until data arrives, saving a wakeup on idle connections; can delay connection-establishment visibility.

fastopen.x-trade-off: Saves an RTT on repeat connections but is spoofable and needs a server-side queue budget.

cork.x-trade-off: Coalesces small writes into full segments at the cost of added per-write latency; wrong for streaming echo.

reuseport.x-trade-off: Enables per-core distribution; set before bind.

rcvbuf.description: SO_RCVBUF per TCP socket, in bytes.
rcvbuf.x-trade-off: Larger absorbs bursts at the cost of memory; the kernel doubles the value it reports.

sndbuf.description: SO_SNDBUF per TCP socket, in bytes.
sndbuf.x-trade-off: Larger absorbs bursts at the cost of memory.

nodelay.x-trade-off: Lowest latency at the cost of more small packets.

init_max_streams.x-trade-off: More streams support more concurrent message flows per association at the cost of per-stream state.

partial_delivery_point.x-trade-off: Smaller delivers partial messages sooner (latency) at the cost of fragmented reads.

max_burst.x-trade-off: Limits packet bursts per association (loss avoidance) at the cost of throughput bursts.

reuseport.x-trade-off: Enables per-core distribution; set before bind.

socket_path.description: Unix socket path for the metrics pull endpoint; empty = disabled.
socket_path.x-trade-off: Pull-based metrics avoid hot-path writes; a filesystem path is a local trust boundary.
socket_path.x-derived-from: engine default ([OBS] pull, not hot-path write)

splice.x-trade-off: Kernel-side copy avoids a userspace bounce for file data; costs a pipe staging when splicing between sockets.

registered_buffers.x-trade-off: Avoids per-op buffer pinning at the cost of registration setup and fixed-buffer bookkeeping.

udp_zerocopy.description: MSG_ZEROCOPY for UDP large datagrams (see also udp.zerocopy).
udp_zerocopy.x-trade-off: Avoids a kernel copy for big buffers at the cost of completion-notification handling and page pinning.

device.description: Device name for AF_XDP (e.g. eth0); empty = disabled.
device.x-trade-off: Kernel-bypass RX/TX on a dedicated queue needs an XDP-capable NIC, CAP_NET_RAW, and a pinned XDP program; absent a device the engine logs and stays on the kernel datapath.

queue.description: Queue id on the AF_XDP device.
queue.x-trade-off: Binding a queue dedicates it to the XDP path.

udp_bind.x-trade-off: Loopback default; bind 0.0.0.0 (or a NIC address) for external traffic.

tcp_bind.x-trade-off: Loopback default; bind 0.0.0.0 for external traffic.
